knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=2 x y z$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨3 u,\,v,\,u v⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨3,\,0,\,v⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\3&0&v\\0&1&u\end{vmatrix}=⟨- v,\,- 3 u,\,3⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(- v\right)^{2}+\left(- 3 u\right)^{2}+\left(3\right)^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{9 u^{2} + v^{2} + 9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 \left(3 u\right) \left(v\right) \left(u v\right)\\&=6 u^{2} v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor:

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D 6 u^{2} v^{2} \sqrt{9 u^{2} + v^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The missing expression is $6 u^{2} v^{2} \sqrt{9 u^{2} + v^{2} + 9}$. The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=2 x - 2 z^{2}$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨u^{3},\,v,\,v^{2}⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨3 u^{2},\,0,\,0⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,1,\,2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\3 u^{2}&0&0\\0&1&2 v\end{vmatrix}=⟨0,\,- 6 u^{2} v,\,3 u^{2}⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(0\right)^{2}+\left(- 6 u^{2} v\right)^{2}+\left(3 u^{2}\right)^{2}}\\&=3 u^{2} \sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=2 \left(u^{3}\right) - 2 \left(v^{2}\right)^{2}\\&=2 u^{3} - 2 v^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor:

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D 3 u^{2} \sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1} \left(2 u^{3} - 2 v^{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The missing expression is $3 u^{2} \sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1} \left(2 u^{3} - 2 v^{4}\right)$. The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Consider $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} z^{2} + 2 y$ on the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=⟨- u,\,- u,\,- v⟩
$$

The parameter region is $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}$. What expression completes the integral? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrized surface, the scalar surface integral is

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate while holding the other parameter fixed:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=⟨-1,\,-1,\,0⟩\\\mathbf r_v&=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Form the cross product, including the negative middle cofactor:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\-1&-1&0\\0&0&-1\end{vmatrix}=⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩.
$$

Take its nonnegative magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{\left(1\right)^{2}+\left(-1\right)^{2}+\left(0\right)^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the coordinates into the scalar function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(- u\right)^{2} \left(- v\right)^{2} + 2 \left(- u\right)\\&=u^{2} v^{2} - 2 u.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiply the substituted scalar function by the area factor:

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D \sqrt{2} \left(u^{2} v^{2} - 2 u\right)\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

The missing expression is $\sqrt{2} \left(u^{2} v^{2} - 2 u\right)$. The magnitude applies to the cross product; the scalar function retains its sign.
